property_summary: For any caller that is the current owner and any new owner address, a successful setOwner(newOwner) must make c.owner() equal newOwner; the mutant never updates owner, so for some fuzzed newOwner c.owner() != newOwner.

For any caller and any candidate address, after setOwner(newOwner) succeeds the contract's owner must equal exactly the address passed in; the buggy version instead sets owner to the caller, breaking this for any newOwner different from the caller.

An ownership transfer actually hands over control: any address nominated by the current owner must subsequently be able to exercise ownership rights (successfully call setOwner), which the reference always permits but the mutant violates because it leaves ownership with the caller, so the nominee's later call reverts.
For any caller other than the owner, setOwner must revert and leave owner unchanged; the mutant with the deleted require lets any caller succeed and change owner.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): setOwner must only succeed for owner

property_summary: For any caller and any argument, setOwner(newOwner) must set owner exactly to newOwner and change nothing else; the mutant instead overwrites owner with msg.sender, so for any caller other than newOwner the resulting owner differs from the requested value.

After any successful ownership transfer to x, a subsequent call to setOwner(y) made by x must succeed and set owner to y; the mutant steals ownership to the first caller, so x's follow-up call reverts.

For any caller and any requested newOwner, a successful setOwner call must end with owner set exactly to the requested newOwner (not silently to the caller); the mutant leaves owner equal to the caller whenever the caller passes any other target, breaking the rule.

For any fuzzed address a different from the current owner, a successful setOwner(a) must revoke the previous owner's privilege so that the previous owner can no longer call setOwner; the mutant silently keeps ownership at the caller, so the previous owner still succeeds.

For any caller authorized as owner and any requested newOwner, a successful setOwner must leave owner exactly equal to the requested newOwner; note, however, that in this mutant the modifier's `owner = msg.sender` is immediately overwritten by the function body's `owner = _owner`, so the observable final state and return values coincide with the reference for every input and no purely external assertion can separate them — the strongest universal rule is asserted below.
For any caller and any address argument, a successful call to setOwner made by the current owner must return true; the buggy version returns false, breaking this rule.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): setOwner called by owner must return true

property_summary: For any address a chosen by the (current) owner, a successful call to setOwner(a) must return true and make c.owner() equal a; the mutant always returns false (and never changes the owner), so it violates this for every admissible input.

For every candidate address including the zero address, the owner can transfer ownership to it and c.owner() equals that address afterwards; the mutant wrongly reverts when the candidate is address(0).

For any address a, the owner's call setOwner(a) succeeds and c.owner() becomes a; the mutant breaks this for a == address(0) by reverting, so the domain is bounded to {0,1} so the zero address is actually reachable by the fuzzer.
For any caller that is the current owner and any address a, calling setOwner(a) must succeed and set c.owner() to a; the buggy contract reverts for such calls, so its owner stays unchanged.
For any caller, setOwner only succeeds when the caller is the current owner (owner can be changed only by the owner); the mutant lets any address succeed and change owner.

For any caller acting as owner and any new owner address, a successful setOwner(newOwner) must set owner to exactly newOwner; the mutant instead sets owner to address(this), violating the rule for any input with newOwner != address(c).

Whoever is set as owner by setOwner can immediately exercise owner rights again (a second setOwner by the same actor succeeds); the mutant makes owner = address(this), so the actor loses control and the second call reverts for every actor != address(c).
For any caller equal to the current owner, setOwner returns true on success; the mutant deletes `return true` so it returns the default false, breaking the rule.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): successful setOwner by owner must return true

property_summary: For any caller equal to the current owner and any non-zero address a, a completed call setOwner(a) must leave the public getter c.owner() equal to a; the mutant always overwrites the owner to address(0), so it violates this for any a != address(0).
